title: Pray for the dead: Bishop Strickland on Purgatory and the holy souls
description: Bringing you the news from a traditional Catholic perspective. During the month of November, after All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day, Bishop Joseph Strickland urges Catholics to pray for the faithful departed. Drawing on Church teaching, he explains that purgatory is the final purification of those who die in God’s grace and friendship but still need to be made completely holy before entering the full communion of heaven. These “holy souls” are assured of salvation. Their suffering is real, but it is temporary and redemptive. … Sodom & the Synod: Why the Church must speak clearly about sin | Bishop Strickland Are we becoming a Church without God? title: Leo’s Vatican forbids bishops from insisting on ad orientem Mass
description: Bringing you the news from a traditional Catholic perspective. The Vatican intervened in the Syro-Malabar Catholic Church in India, with the Apostolic Signatura reportedly siding with priests who wanted to celebrate Mass facing the congregation rather than ad orientem despite their bishops’ direction. John-Henry Westen argues the decision raises questions about the Vatican’s treatment of traditional liturgical practices beyond the Latin Mass. The same Vatican that promotes a “carbon fast” during Lent now overrules bishops who want their priests facing East. … Is this why Fr. title: Pro-lifers welcome news that Carney’s budget leaves pregnancy centers untouched
description: OTTAWA ( LifeSiteNews ) — Canada’s leading pro-life group, Campaign Life Coalition (CLC), says it is glad that the 2026 Liberal federal government’s budget did not follow through on a recommendation to “penalize” pro-life pregnancy centers. “We thank God,” said CLC’s National President Jeff Gunnarson in a press release sent to LifeSiteNews. … According to CLC, since abortion became legal in Canada in 1969, nearly five million preborn children have “been erased” by the deadly practice. The grim truth is that abortion has become more common in Canada. There were 368,928 babies born in Canada from 2024 to 2025, a number that would be much greater if not for abortion. In 2022, 97,211 Canadian babies were killed by abortion. Similarly, reports from 2018 indicated that 766 babies were born alive and presumably left to die after late-term abortions in Canada between 2013 and 2018.
